title: Hereditary Name
text: “By the way, night views and such are pretty, but… the night sea where you can only see starlight was pretty too. There’s something about it that just pulls you in, you know?”

For some reason, Ark suddenly came to mind. Father had been talking a little about the place where he’d met Ark. If I recalled correctly, it was some place that seemed to have been destroyed by waves, where countless different worlds could be seen like stars. Perhaps it was a starry sky… no, perhaps it was more like some kind of outer space. Was Ark still traveling through a place like that even now? I felt at ease imagining Hou-kun flying through such places without hesitation, but I worried about Ark calmly trudging onward through them.
“Well, doesn’t look like anything’s going to happen today, so I suppose I’ll be heading out soon myself.”
“You’re not going to go rampaging around Melromarc again, are you?”

“Don’t worry, it won’t be anything like that. Since it’s only the day after yesterday, I’ll just be stretching my wings a bit. Somehow, whenever I’m around Naofumi-san, I end up complaining and leaning on you too much.”
“There’s a limit, but it’s fine to lean on me, you know.”
“Yes, I’m counting on you. Well then.”
And with that, Itsuki decided on something of his own and headed out.
“Hm? Wait, is that… Gaelion?”

As everyone was going their separate ways like that… the parent who normally resided in Rival’s body, always glued to Assistant, was standing there today in an unnatural way, and approached looking toward Father and me. …This one! This wasn’t the parent dwelling in Rival’s body! This was Rival herself, I say. After such a long acquaintance, I’d gotten to where I could spot it in an instant. What was the meaning of standing so brazenly before us like this? Or rather, I had all sorts of things I wanted to say—why did it look different from yesterday, had there been some kind of switch, and so on.
“…? You… aren’t you different from Wyndia-chan’s father?”
At that, Rival floated up lightly and gave an affected, stylish bow.
“Sharp as ever, nano. As expected of Naofumi, nano. Gaelion is Gaelion, nano.”
“No, the name hasn’t changed.”

“Even so, since it’s a name that’s been inherited, it’s the same name, nano. Gaelion is the Gaelion who exists looping alongside the Spear Hero and Raph, same as always—the daughter of the Gaelion this loop’s Naofumi knows, and the original owner of this body, nano.”
“So it’s a hereditary name, and it’s the same-named person from a different loop? That’s confusing.”

“If you absolutely must call it something different, Gaelion-chan is fine too, nano. Other Naofumis have called it Mesulion before, so it’s fine to go by that this time too, nano. There was also a younger brother with the same name as Gaelion, so it was to tell them apart, nano.”
“Wow, you’re surprisingly flexible about that.”
“Father! Be careful, I say! This one’s ambition is your virginity, indeed! It’s already been stolen from you once!”
When I added that supplement, Father narrowed his eyes and looked at me.
“Ah… so that’s why she kept making a fuss about me needing to graduate from virginity whenever something happened. It was because of this kid?”

“Ever since the loop where Gaelion and Naofumi became mutually in love, nano, it hasn’t even been a target anymore, but it’s held a grudge across the ages regardless, nano. Honestly getting sick of it by now, nano.”
“Sounds like once Motoyasu-kun holds a grudge, it runs deep.”
“Don’t get close, Father! What could it possibly be scheming to come out so brazenly like this, I wonder! Shouldn’t it be preparing more thoroughly?”
“Nobody said anything like that, nano.”
Just what in the world was it plotting this time to come out so boldly!—or so I was thinking, when Raph, in her true form, showed up as well.
“And so, my senior and the natural enemy of Spear Hero makes her official appearance. Fufufu… you’ve shown me quite the entertaining sight.”
Raph, looking rather satisfied, spoke as if introducing Rival. Rival, in contrast, let out a deep sigh.

“Y-you seem to be suffering some kind of damage from Raph-chan. Well, setting that aside, it’s impressive you managed to stay together with Ren and Wyndia-chan without them noticing. Or rather, where’s Gaelion-san?”
“That part needs explaining in order too, nano. First, regarding Sword Hero…”
Rival stared fixedly at me and Raph as though looking at something troublesome, then averted her gaze and turned to face Father.

“Explaining that part would be a tangent, so I’ll save it for later. As for how I managed to pass myself off, I extracted information from Gaelion’s parent and there’s years of accumulated experience too, so it wasn’t especially difficult, nano. Rather… haaaaaaah.”
Rival let out a long, deep sigh. Her mood seemed quite low.
“What’s wrong?”

“I’ll let it slide that all sorts of things have already gone wrong from the very start this loop, but as for this particular matter, I honestly have no words other than that it was genuinely disgusting, nano.”
“Fufufufu… the look on your face when you understood your situation was quite comical. It rivaled the shock on the face of a small pet monster when its owner cleans out its precious nest.”
Raph seemed to be in rather good spirits.
“What’s with that phrasing, like some pet owner enjoying the reaction of cleaning a hamster’s nest while it was out?… What actually happened?”

“Well, Naofumi, I want you to understand—when Gaelion loops, it’s not desirable for there to be multiple Gaelions, so all sorts of adjustments get made so that Gaelion’s own egg doesn’t hatch, rigged so it can be swapped out later, nano.”
Here, Rival explained to Father that whenever she looped, she rigged things through me so that her own egg wouldn’t hatch. Apparently the egg’s soul was drawn away and hatched somewhere else instead.
“Ah, so the reason the egg entrusted to Wyndia-chan wasn’t hatching was because of you.”

“Nano. And yet, of all things, I was shown the disgusting sight of my own parent using Gaelion’s body, nano. A revulsion welled up in me at my father’s feminine speech, unbidden, nano. Honestly… forcibly breaking through the lock and pulling off something so outrageous, nano.”
“Hmm… would that be something like the revulsion of a father breaking into his teenage daughter’s locked room without permission, only to find him cross-dressing in her school uniform?”

Ugh… I’d had zero intention of ever understanding anything about Rival, but Father’s all-too-specific example gave even me a chill—or rather, a wave of disgust—welling up unbidden. Somehow… I felt like there’d been a similarly deranged parent back in the Japan I once lived in. Everyone around treated it as a joke, but I got the feeling that for the pig involved and for me, it had genuinely been an appalling affair. A bit of sympathy for Rival began to well up in me.
“So then, where’s your parent now?”

“Well, I watched for an opening, took back control of the body, then crystallized and sealed it away, nano. In the process, I drew out the memories from after hatching in this loop directly from the body, and have been continuing on cooperating with the sisters ever since, nano.”
And with that… Rival, with practiced ease, showed us the crystal in which her parent was apparently sealed.
“So Wyndia-chan’s father is in there?”
“The pervert who’s also Gaelion’s parent, nano.”
“I’d appreciate it if you didn’t mind that too much—Motoyasu and the others already give him a hard time about it, so—”
“Still a pervert, nano. A pathetic dragon emperor who can never graduate from being a big sister!”
“Hmm… well, the owner of the body’s gotten angry at him, but… since he had no way of knowing about the looping, I can’t help but feel that’s a bit unreasonable.”
“It’s fine, nano—Gaelion will process it properly afterward so he won’t have to use feminine speech anymore, nano.”
She was probably going to compact him again. Even I could tell. It was Rival’s specialty technique, after all.
“You mean this, don’t you?”
Raph tossed over a compact I recognized at a glance.
